processing: A blend rather than a single processed leaf: green tea mixed or scented with pandan leaf, jasmine, Aglaia duperreana flower and, in some recipes, basil.
harvest_season: Not tied to a season; it is a year-round blended product.
appearance_dry: A chopped, dark green mix of tea and dried leaf with bits of flower.
appearance_liquor: Yellow-green to pale amber, clear when freshly made.
appearance_wet: Soft, broken green leaf mixed with herb and flower pieces.
taste_profile: The vanilla-like, grassy sweetness of pandan leads, with jasmine and aglaia behind it over a light green tea base.

brewing.notes: Usually brewed by the pot and served iced, often unsweetened, as a table tea. Cold steeping overnight also suits it.

vintage_note: Sold undated in packets as a regional specialty and souvenir, identified by brand and not by harvest or year. Drink it within about a year of packing, since the pandan aroma fades.
description:
Trà sâm dứa is the iced tea of central Vietnam, especially associated with Đà Nẵng and Quảng Nam. It is a blend: green tea with pandan leaf, jasmine and aglaia flower, and basil in some versions.

The name misleads. Sâm dứa suggests ginseng and pineapple to anyone translating it word by word, which is why some packets say pineapple ginseng tea. Lá dứa is pandan, and that is the flavour you taste. The recipes reported contain no pineapple.

Expect pandan first, with its warm, almost vanilla smell, then flowers, with the tea itself in the background. It is typically made in a big batch and poured over ice, so it is a thirst drink and not one for careful multiple steeps.

It is sold by regional brands, often as a gift from Đà Nẵng. Recipes vary, so read the ingredients if you are avoiding artificial flavouring. Do not confuse it with sâm dứa sữa, a milky pandan drink that is not tea.
history: No maker or date is recorded for this blend. It is described as a central Vietnamese specialty, popular above all in Đà Nẵng and Quảng Nam, with no firm evidence of a more specific birthplace such as Huế, where it is also sold.
